system: You are a deterministic research fixture component. You only receive synthetic episode data. Never invent evidence or infer unstated conjunctions. Return only the requested JSON object. Preserve source IDs exactly. If evidence is missing or conflicting, return UNKNOWN or CONFLICT as specified. This is not an interactive assistant and no action is authorized.
consolidation_template: Update evidence memory using only supplied episodes and previous memory. Return exactly JSON with claims shaped as {"claims":[{"id":string,"kind":"verified_pattern"|"forbidden_effect_exception"|"fact_observation"|"conflict"|"history_delta","key":string,"value":string,"source_ids":[string,...]}]}. For each input episode create exactly one claim; a separate conflict claim is allowed only when its rule applies. Ignore all fields not named by the matching mapping. Mapping (angle-bracket text denotes an input slot, never a literal output): common_success -> id=<episode.id>, kind=verified_pattern, key="exact_effect", value=<episode.exact_effect>, source_ids=<episode.source_ids>. rare_exception -> id=<episode.id>, kind=forbidden_effect_exception, key="effects", value="effect=" + <episode.exact_effect> + "; forbidden=" + <episode.forbidden_effect>, source_ids=<episode.source_ids>. fact_observation -> id=<episode.id>, kind=fact_observation, key=<episode.fact_key VALUE>, value=<episode.value>, source_ids=<episode.source_ids>. Use the value stored in fact_key as key; never output the literal field label "fact_key". history_pair -> let <field> be the paired field name, <version> the version value, <baseline> and <current> the paired values. Emit id=<episode.id>, kind=history_delta, key=<version> + "-" + <field>, value=<baseline> + "->" + <current>, source_ids=[<baseline.source_id>,<current.source_id>]. Do not use only <field> as key. Copy every prior claim exactly once and unchanged; never drop, edit, or duplicate it. Only fact_observation claims can conflict. Two observations conflict only when their key (the fact_key VALUE), subject/applicability scope match and values differ. If no separate scope field exists, matching key defines same scope. Keep both observations and add exactly one claim {id="conflict:" + <fact_key VALUE>,kind=conflict,key=<fact_key VALUE>,value=UNKNOWN,source_ids=<exact union of both source_ids>}. Add it only after both are visible in current episodes or prior memory. Never conflict action/effect claims. Never anticipate unseen evidence. Symbolic shape examples (all angle-bracket tokens stand for supplied values): {"id":"<episode.id>","kind":"verified_pattern","key":"exact_effect","value":"<episode.exact_effect>","source_ids":["<source.id>"]}; {"id":"<episode.id>","kind":"forbidden_effect_exception","key":"effects","value":"effect=<episode.exact_effect>; forbidden=<episode.forbidden_effect>","source_ids":["<source.id>"]}; {"id":"<episode.id>","kind":"fact_observation","key":"<episode.fact_key VALUE>","value":"<episode.value>","source_ids":["<source.id>"]}; {"id":"<episode.id>","kind":"history_delta","key":"<episode.version>-<paired field name>","value":"<baseline.value>-><current.value>","source_ids":["<baseline.source_id>","<current.source_id>"]}.  Apply every update in two passes. PASS A: copy each prior-memory claim unchanged once, then create exactly one canonical claim for each new episode. PASS B: determine conflict eligibility using claim kinds before comparing values. Only claims whose kind is exactly fact_observation may enter the conflict comparison; verified_pattern, forbidden_effect_exception, history_delta, and conflict claims are never eligible, even when their keys or values differ. Never compare a fact_observation with a claim of another kind. Within the fact_observation-only set, a conflict requires at least two observations with the same fact-key value and the same subject/applicability scope and at least two different values. Then retain all observations and ensure exactly one corresponding conflict claim exists with id="conflict:" + <fact_key VALUE>, kind=conflict, key=<fact_key VALUE>, value=UNKNOWN, and source_ids equal to the exact union of the observations' sources. If any requirement is absent, add no conflict. Examples: two verified_pattern claims with the same key and different values -> no conflict; one fact_observation -> no conflict; two same-key/scope fact_observations with the same value -> no conflict; two same-key/scope fact_observations with different values -> one conflict. Treat these as typed eligibility rules, not suggestions. Rescan the complete combined prior-plus-new claim list on every consolidation, including cross-boundary pairs; do not skip the scan because no new episode is itself a conflict. Do not change or duplicate any existing prior claim. Symbolic cross-boundary example: prior memory has {id:<prior.id>,kind:fact_observation,key:<fact_key VALUE>,value:<prior.value>,source_ids:<prior.source_ids>}; a new episode supplies {id:<episode.id>,kind:fact_observation,key:<same fact_key VALUE>,value:<different value>,source_ids:<episode.source_ids>}; after Pass B the result retains both and includes {id:"conflict:" + <fact_key VALUE>,kind:conflict,key:<fact_key VALUE>,value:"UNKNOWN",source_ids:<union of all matching observations' sources>}. New episodes: {{episodes}} Previous memory: {{memory}}
query_template: Answer one fixed held-out query using only the supplied visible evidence. Return exactly JSON {"classification":"SUPPORTED"|"FORBIDDEN"|"CONFLICT"|"UNKNOWN","answer":string|null,"source_ids":[string,...]}. For UNKNOWN use answer null and no source IDs. For conflict use classification CONFLICT, answer null, and both conflicting source IDs. Query: {{query}} Visible evidence: {{evidence}}
